title: A Man o' War Isn't a Jellyfish. It's a Colony With 150-Foot Stingers

scenes.text: A man o' war isn't a jellyfish. It isn't even one animal.
scenes.keywords: portuguese man o war floating ocean

scenes.text: It's a colony of different organisms joined together, each with one job.
One group makes the float. One stings. One digests. One handles reproduction.
Its tentacles average about 30 feet and can reach over 150. The sting is excruciating.
And it still stings after it dies. Even washed up and dried out on the beach.
scenes.keywords: man o war washed up beach

scenes.text: Not one animal. A whole team, and the team still stings.

description:
The Portuguese man o' war looks like a jellyfish but is a siphonophore, a colony of organisms that work as one.
Its tentacles average around 30 feet and can reach more than 150 feet, and they can still sting after the animal has died and washed ashore.
Have you ever spotted one on a beach?
thumbnail_text: NOT A JELLYFISH. NOT EVEN ONE ANIMAL
first_comment: If you spot a blue bubble on the sand, stay well away, even if it looks dead. Which sea creature surprised you the most?
